annotation.title_clean: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC
annotation.title_en: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: The revised EU Product Liability Directive establishes no-fault liability of economic operators for damage caused by defective products, expressly extending to software, AI systems, related digital services and self-learning products. It eases claimants' evidence burden through disclosure duties and rebuttable presumptions, and repeals Directive 85/374/EEC from 9 December 2026.
key_provisions_or_claims: Software, including AI systems, digital manufacturing files and related services are 'products' subject to strict liability.
Defectiveness assessment considers self-learning ability, interconnected products, cybersecurity requirements and manufacturer control after market placement.
Court-ordered disclosure of evidence and rebuttable presumptions of defect and causation ease claimants' burden in technically complex cases.
Manufacturers remain liable for defects from software updates, lack of security updates, or substantial modifications within their control.
Applies to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026; liability cannot be contractually limited; 10-year expiry (25 years for latent injury).
